props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the switch is on. An ARIA-mirroring boolean, so the ARIA name verbatim (ADR-013, decision 1) — not `isOn`.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Initial state for the uncontrolled case.

props.name: description
props.description: Persistent helper text below the row.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables interaction. Mirrors the ARIA name.

props.name: error
props.description: The validation message. Its presence drives `aria-invalid`.

props.name: form
props.description: Associates the control with a form it is not nested inside.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the field invalid, with the same independence from `error` as Checkbox.

props.name: label
props.description: The label text, rendered beside the track. Wraps the control.

props.name: required
props.description: Native constraint validation still applies and is never suppressed.

props.name: size
props.description: Label text size. The row target stays 44px at every size.

props.name: value
props.description: The submitted value when on. `"on"` is the platform default, kept so a plain form reads exactly what a native checkbox-role=switch would send.

props.name: name
props.description: The name of the element, used when submitting an HTML form.

ai.summary: An on/off control that acts immediately, rendered as a native checkbox carrying role=switch so the browser keeps validation and form submission.
whenToUse: The setting applies the moment it is toggled — a preference, a visibility toggle
The state is genuinely binary: on or off, with no third state
It must submit through a plain `<form>` with no JavaScript state
whenNotToUse: The choice is collected for a later submit — use a Checkbox
The choice is one of several exclusive options — use a Radio Group
The action triggers something rather than setting a state — use a Button
ai.accessibility: Renders a real native `<input type="checkbox">` carrying `role="switch"`, so the browser supplies constraint validation, Space-to-toggle, and autofill while assistive technology reads the state as on/off. The label wraps the input, making the whole row the activation target with no click handler. `label`, `description`, and `error` are wired through the wrapping label and `aria-describedby`; an error sets `aria-invalid` and renders an icon beside its text, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Implements the FACE contract: formResetCallback, formDisabledCallback, formStateRestoreCallback, and sk-value-change fires only for user-initiated changes.
knownLimitations: The generated `id` for the inner control differs from React's `useId()`, so an SSR consumer must pass an explicit `id` for a separately-rendered `Label` to find it (section 4, forms contract)
